selection_standard: KEEP unless a panel has a catastrophic identity, disability, anatomy, or scene-meaning failure
style: sketch-forward graphite and selective ink with restrained loose pigment on warm paper

items.title: THE OWNER
items.anchor: Antonius was already cleaning when I arrived
items.alt: Antonius carries a crate through the crowded storeroom while Greg studies metal pieces at a workbench.

items.title: THE WITNESS
items.anchor: The dead creatures were under canvas
items.alt: A butcher lifts canvas from a dead strange creature in the busy watch yard as Greg and Alden observe.

items.title: THE REPORTER
items.anchor: The woman placed two fingers against the stone
items.alt: A stoneworker splits a block cleanly at Hessa's worktable while Greg watches.

items.title: THE SIGNAL
items.anchor: The south freight spur smelled like wet stone
items.alt: Greg raises the hold marker beside a loaded cart at the wet drain-crossing repair.

items.title: THE EXTRA HAND
items.anchor: Then someone hit me in the shoulder with a padded stick
items.alt: Alden knocks Greg off balance during fast padded sparring in the practice yard.

items.title: THE REGULAR
items.anchor: I walked.
items.alt: Greg advances on his crutches while forming a small angled Barrier under Hessa's supervision.

items.title: THE SURVEYOR
items.anchor: A farm approach crossed a shallow roadside ditch
items.alt: Greg examines water and debris at a rain-cut culvert while Pessa's wagon waits nearby.

items.title: THE INSPECTOR
items.anchor: A farm cart approached from behind us
items.alt: Greg stops an approaching farm cart as Pessa probes the wet road shoulder from firm ground.

items.title: THE BACKSTOP
items.anchor: Clearance support for a heavy frame moving from river barge to yard cart
items.alt: Greg watches a hoist shift a huge mill frame from a river barge toward a reinforced yard cart.

items.title: THE REACHER
items.anchor: And from the top of the frame hung a single dark thread
items.alt: Hessa watches a single suspended thread beside Greg's supported right forearm during the bounded assessment.

items.title: THE ERRAND
items.anchor: Lyssa found me buying pears
items.alt: Lyssa and Greg move through a crowded market crossing with pears and folded cloth in hand.

items.title: THE HORSE
items.anchor: The soot-shirt worker returned dragging a narrow board
items.alt: The theatre company creates a horse entrance with gray cloth and a hoof board while Greg watches from the side.

items.title: THE TEST CASE
items.anchor: Hessa had two threads
items.alt: Hessa records the motion of two suspended threads while Greg holds his forearm still at the assessment table.

items.title: THE OLD ROAD
items.anchor: Not Guild cart. Courier cart.
items.alt: Sevren works beneath a long courier cart with its wheel cap removed while Greg watches from the wet Guild steps.

items.title: THE REPEAT
items.anchor: She opened the door. Waited. Both threads moved.
items.alt: Hessa opens the assessment-room door and watches the differently sleeved threads move while Greg observes.

items.title: THE MESSENGER
items.anchor: Second attempt. Correct blue door.
items.alt: Greg crosses the rehearsal stage on crutches carrying a prop letter toward the blue door.

items.title: THE LIMIT
items.anchor: No thread. No fixed destination. Just direction.
items.alt: Hessa points through the empty air over Greg's supported forearm for a direction-only assessment.

items.title: THE EXTRA
items.anchor: The scene involved three people at a supper table
items.alt: Actors wage a chaotic silent struggle over supper-table objects while Greg watches the rehearsal from the side.

items.title: THE DIRECTION
items.anchor: She reached for a narrow folded towel
items.alt: Hessa adjusts the towel beneath Greg's forearm during the direction-first wristward assessment.

items.title: THE HOUR
items.anchor: Lyssa pulled the cart over the curb edge
items.alt: Lyssa rocks a loaded handcart wheel free from the curb while Greg moves around to help.

items.title: THE OTHER WAY
items.anchor: It is a legendary sword
items.alt: A soot-shirted theatre worker raises the ridiculous legendary sword as the company argues and Greg arrives.

items.title: THE VOICE
items.anchor: The fake red stone caught light
items.alt: The servant actor points the silver-painted sword with its red stone toward Greg as Greg supplies the voice.

items.title: THE REPEAT
items.anchor: speaking to the king while two soldiers tried to open a stone door
items.alt: The talking-sword scene unfolds as a king and two soldiers struggle at a stone stage door while Greg voices the sword.

items.title: THE OLD VOICE
items.anchor: Inside, the servant actor was already holding the sword
items.alt: The servant actor reacts mid-scene with the old sword while Greg times its voice from the side of the stage.

items.title: THE SHAPE
items.anchor: I took the charcoal. Not magic. Ordinary.
items.alt: Greg draws an uneven oval from memory in charcoal while Hessa labels the assessment sheet.
